Reasoning: According to the method, label the vertices of the regular hexagon clockwise as A=upper left, B=upper right, C=right, D=lower right, E=lower left, F=left, and let the side length be s. The three shaded triangles of X are respectively △FAB, △FED, △BCD; each is formed by two adjacent sides, with included angle 120°, and area (1/2)s^2 sin120° = √3 s^2/4, so X = 3√3 s^2/4. Y is divided by the center into 6 congruent equilateral triangles, each with area √3 s^2/4, and the shading is 3 of them, so Y = 3√3 s^2/4. The shading of Z is △FBD; all three sides are long diagonals skipping one vertex, with length √3s, so the area is (√3/4)(√3s)^2 = 3√3 s^2/4. Thus the areas X, Y, Z are equal.

method.method_draft: Label the vertices of a regular hexagon clockwise as A=upper-left, B=upper-right, C=right, D=lower-right, E=lower-left, F=left. From the image, X shades triangles FAB, FED, and BCD; Y shades three center-to-adjacent-vertices sectors; Z shades the large triangle FBD. Let the common side length be s. In a regular hexagon, adjacent sides meet at 120°, so each of the three shaded corner triangles in X has area (1/2)s^2 sin 120° = sqrt(3)s^2/4, giving X=3sqrt(3)s^2/4. For Y, the hexagon is split by radii into six congruent equilateral triangles of side s, and exactly three are shaded, so Y=3sqrt(3)s^2/4. For Z, FBD is an equilateral triangle whose side is the long diagonal between alternate vertices, sqrt(3)s, so its area is (sqrt(3)/4)(sqrt(3)s)^2=3sqrt(3)s^2/4. Therefore X=Y=Z.
